transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been having this... this issue at work. I'm a construction manager, and lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or any kind of upper platform, my head just tells me I'm about to go over. It doesn't matter that I can see the rails are in place, or that I know the setup is supposed to be safe. The feeling is just completely overwhelming.
When you're near a scaffold, roof edge, or upper platform, do you experience symptoms like rapid heartbeat, sweating, trembling, or a feeling of losing control?

Yeah, definitely. The second I step onto temporary stairs or even just walk toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens up. My hands get all wet and sweaty, and... honestly, I feel like my legs might just lock up completely before I can even make myself take another step. It's an immediate reaction.
Do you experience these symptoms only when you're near heights, such as scaffolds or roof edges, or do you also have similar reactions in other situations that aren't related to being up high?

No, it's really just the heights. If I'm down on the ground, I'm completely fine. I mean, I could be dealing with a chaotic site, heavy machinery, tight deadlines, whatever... and I don't get that panic at all. It's strictly when I have to go up or get near a drop-off.
When you feel that panic coming on near a height, do you find yourself actively avoiding those situations, like refusing to go up or making someone else handle tasks up high?

Yeah, I do. I mean, lately I've been handing off a lot of the height inspections to my foremen. I'll also move any meetings we have down to the ground level just so I don't have to deal with it. 

But sometimes I can't get out of it. When I absolutely have to go up there, I make sure to keep someone right beside me. And even then, I just rush through the work as fast as I can, basically scared the whole time I'm up there.
